quests.sentence: The reports are reviewed every month.
quests.ruleExplanation: The reports (the thing acted upon) becomes the subject, followed by are reviewed — the passive shifts focus from who reviews to what gets reviewed.
quests.nativeTip: The thing receiving the action becomes the subject, followed by is/are plus the past participle.

quests.sentence: English is spoken in many countries.
quests.ruleExplanation: English is spoken shifts focus onto the language itself rather than any specific speaker, which is why no agent is mentioned.
quests.nativeTip: The passive works well when the doer is unimportant or unknown — here, who speaks English isn't the point.

quests.sentence: The packages are delivered by the courier.
quests.ruleExplanation: By the courier names the agent doing the delivering, following are delivered — the passive form still allows the agent when it's relevant.
quests.nativeTip: By plus the doer can still follow the past participle when the agent is worth naming.

quests.sentence: The building was designed by a famous architect.
quests.ruleExplanation: Was designed uses the past passive form, and by a famous architect names an agent worth mentioning because it adds important information.
quests.nativeTip: The past passive uses was/were plus the past participle, with by naming a specific, notable agent.

quests.sentence: The contract was signed yesterday.
quests.ruleExplanation: Was signed uses the past passive form, with yesterday (time) closing the sentence instead of a by-agent.
quests.nativeTip: The past passive can also close with a time word instead of an agent.

quests.sentence: The results were announced this morning.
quests.ruleExplanation: Were announced pairs the plural subject the results with the past passive form, followed by this morning (time).
quests.nativeTip: Were pairs with a plural subject in the past passive, the same way was does for singular.

quests.sentence: The novel was written by a young author.
quests.ruleExplanation: By a young author is included because knowing who wrote the novel matters to the reader — the agent is worth naming here.
quests.nativeTip: Include the by-agent when knowing who did the action adds real, useful information.

quests.sentence: The window was broken.
quests.ruleExplanation: Was broken has no by-agent at all, since who broke the window is unknown or unimportant — the passive lets the sentence work without one.
quests.nativeTip: Omit the by-agent entirely when the doer is unknown or simply doesn't matter.

quests.sentence: The award was presented by the mayor.
quests.ruleExplanation: By the mayor is included because the presenter's identity matters, following was presented in the passive form.
quests.nativeTip: Include the agent again here, since knowing who presented the award is meaningful information.

quests.sentence: The form must be submitted by Friday.
quests.ruleExplanation: Must be submitted inserts be right after the modal must, before the past participle submitted — modals always take be, never is/was, in the passive.
quests.nativeTip: A modal like must is followed by be plus the past participle, not is or was.

quests.sentence: This medicine should be taken with food.
quests.ruleExplanation: Should be taken inserts be after should, before the past participle taken, following the fixed modal-passive pattern.
quests.nativeTip: The same modal-be-participle pattern applies with should, for advice.

quests.sentence: The issue can be resolved quickly.
quests.ruleExplanation: Can be resolved inserts be after can, before resolved, with quickly (manner) closing the sentence.
quests.nativeTip: Can also takes be plus the past participle in the passive, expressing ability or possibility.

quests.conceptTitle: Present Perfect Passive (Has/Have + Been + Past Participle)
quests.sentence: The proposal has been finished.
quests.ruleExplanation: Has been finished stacks has, been, and finished in that fixed order, linking a completed action to the present moment.
quests.nativeTip: Present perfect passive combines has/have with been, then the past participle — three parts in that order.

quests.conceptTitle: Present Perfect Passive (Has/Have + Been + Past Participle)
quests.sentence: The documents have been reviewed.
quests.ruleExplanation: Have been reviewed stacks have, been, and reviewed for the plural subject the documents.
quests.nativeTip: Have pairs with been the same way for a plural subject.

quests.conceptTitle: Present Perfect Passive (Has/Have + Been + Past Participle)
quests.sentence: The building has been renovated recently.
quests.ruleExplanation: Has been renovated stacks has, been, and renovated, with recently closing the sentence.
quests.nativeTip: The same three-part structure holds, with a time adverb closing the sentence.

quests.sentence: The email was not sent.
quests.ruleExplanation: Was not sent places not between was and the past participle sent, negating the passive action.
quests.nativeTip: Not slots in between was and the past participle, the same spot it takes in active be-negatives.

quests.sentence: The changes weren't approved.
quests.ruleExplanation: Weren't approved fuses were and not into one word, right before the past participle approved.
quests.nativeTip: Weren't fuses were and not, still sitting right before the past participle.

quests.sentence: The order hasn't been shipped yet.
quests.ruleExplanation: Hasn't been shipped combines the negative present-perfect-passive form, with yet closing the sentence to emphasize it still hasn't happened.
quests.nativeTip: Hasn't been combines the negative contraction with been, before the past participle, plus yet at the end.

quests.sentence: Was the report finished on time?
quests.ruleExplanation: Was moves ahead of the report to form the question, with finished on time following in normal passive order.
quests.nativeTip: Move was to the front of the sentence, ahead of the subject, to ask the passive question.

quests.sentence: Is the software updated regularly?
quests.ruleExplanation: Is opens the question before the software, with updated regularly completing it.
quests.nativeTip: Is inverts the same way for present passive questions, with the manner adverb at the end.

quests.sentence: Has the invoice been paid?
quests.ruleExplanation: Has opens the question before the invoice, with been paid completing the present-perfect-passive question.
quests.nativeTip: Has inverts to the front for a present-perfect-passive question, before been and the past participle.

quests.sentence: When was the decision made?
quests.ruleExplanation: When opens the question, was follows, the decision is the subject, and made completes the passive question.
quests.nativeTip: The question word leads, then was, then the subject, then the past participle.

quests.sentence: Where was this photo taken?
quests.ruleExplanation: Where leads the question, was follows, this photo is the subject, and taken completes it.
quests.nativeTip: Where comes first, then was, then the subject, then the past participle.

quests.sentence: Why was the meeting postponed?
quests.ruleExplanation: Why leads the question, was follows, the meeting is the subject, and postponed completes it.
quests.nativeTip: Why still opens the question, followed by was, the subject, and the past participle.

quests.sentence: The company laid off fifty employees.
quests.ruleExplanation: The company (the doer) is the subject here, acting directly on fifty employees — this is the active voice, focusing on who did the action.
quests.nativeTip: An active sentence puts the doer first, as the subject, right before the verb.

quests.sentence: Fifty employees were laid off.
quests.ruleExplanation: Fifty employees (the receiver of the action) becomes the subject here, with the doer the company dropped entirely — a natural passive choice when the affected people matter more than who did it.
quests.nativeTip: The passive version puts the receiver of the action first instead, dropping the agent entirely.

quests.sentence: The proposal was rejected by the board.
quests.ruleExplanation: By the board names the agent who rejected the proposal, showing the passive can include an agent when it's still relevant information.
quests.nativeTip: The passive can also keep the agent, when naming who made the decision still matters.

quests.sentence: All applications must be submitted before the deadline.
quests.ruleExplanation: Must be submitted uses the modal-passive pattern, with before the deadline closing the sentence as the time limit.
quests.nativeTip: Combine a modal passive with a before-time deadline at the end.

quests.sentence: The new policy has been approved by senior management.
quests.ruleExplanation: Has been approved uses the present-perfect-passive pattern, with by senior management naming the agent, typical of formal workplace language.
quests.nativeTip: Combine present perfect passive with a by-agent, common in formal workplace announcements.

quests.sentence: Was the shipment delayed because of bad weather?
quests.ruleExplanation: Was delayed inverts to form the question, with because of bad weather explaining the reason at the end.
quests.nativeTip: Combine a passive question with a because-of reason phrase at the end.
